articles.title: Eighty yards to stay unbeaten
articles.dek: Accel BeckhmJr caught the winner, Electric Berry took away the answer, and Mossdeep survived Saffron 20–17. A second-half shutout came with a painful cost: Marshall Flock is out five weeks.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Mossdeep had to play another fourth quarter that could spoil everything. Good. After the recent blowouts, I wanted to see what this offense would do when the next touchdown was necessary, the opposing pass rush had already made its point, and the running back couldn't spend the afternoon collecting short scores. The answer was an eighty-yard drive, Accel BeckhmJr in the end zone with forty-nine seconds left, and a 20–17 victory over Saffron.

That doesn't make the first half disappear. The Eclipse trailed 17–6 at the break. Medicham sacked Dram Marino four times, all before the middle of the third quarter. Saffron had the more productive passing afternoon and finished with a 334–314 advantage in total yards. This was a difficult opponent playing well enough to win. Mossdeep stayed unbeaten because it eventually completed the work its first-half possessions had left unfinished, while its defense stopped allowing Saffron to finish anything.

Michael Dorrill's team is 9–0. Trent Scarboro's Psi Corps fell to 7–2, their seven-game winning streak over. BeckhmJr caught eight passes for 117 yards and both Eclipse touchdowns. Electric Berry recovered a fumble, then intercepted Archam Manning's first throw after the winning score. Those two players supply the clean headline. Marshall Flock's five-week injury supplies the part nobody can celebrate away.

body.speaker: Accel BeckhmJr
body.text: I would've preferred to make everybody comfortable a little earlier. Apparently we were doing suspense this week. Dram kept coming back to me, and the last one was the one we had to have.
Saffron made the early possessions count

The visitors' first touchdown required actual work: nine plays and eighty yards. Manning converted third-and-seven with a deep-left throw to Dam Skattebo for twenty-four yards, then third-and-eight with a nine-yard short-left completion to Gengar Pickens. On the next snap he went deep left to Pickens again, this time for a thirty-yard touchdown with forty seconds left in the opening quarter. The scoring play was the reward for surviving the two difficult downs before it.

Mossdeep responded with a long possession of its own. BeckhmJr converted third-and-ten for twenty-seven yards; Lorenzo Steel later gained sixteen on third-and-four. Then Medicham sacked Marino for six yards, and the drive stalled. Adam Vinathorn's forty-yard field goal made it 7–3. I liked the conversions. I disliked the ending. Against Saffron, driving close enough to admire the end zone was not going to be sufficient.

The Psi Corps went seventy-five yards in eleven plays on their next possession. Skattebo and Emmitt Smoth contributed useful runs, Gorebyss caught two passes, and Manning spread the ball without giving the drive away. Pawmo caught the three-yard touchdown on a short-left throw with 1:22 remaining in the half. Saffron had twice built a touchdown drive of at least seventy-five yards. It wasn't living on one fortunate bounce.

Ninjulio Jones' forty-four-yard kickoff return gave Mossdeep a chance to answer quickly. Instead, Medicham recorded consecutive sacks, losses of seven and five yards. Gronkaludon's eighteen-yard catch on third-and-twenty-two salvaged kicking range, and Vinathorn's forty-seven-yarder went in off the upright. The kicker had six points. The offense had two separate reasons to thank him.

Saffron still found time for a seventy-yard drive and Vikavolt's twenty-seven-yard field goal. Pickens supplied the biggest gain, forty-eight yards down the left side with eighteen seconds on the clock. Manning went to halftime with the lead and evidence that Mossdeep's secondary could be stretched. Pickens finished with four catches for 107 yards. Any account that turns Saffron into an undeserving loser has misplaced the entire first half.

body.speaker: Trent Scarboro
body.text: We put ourselves in position to finish a good win. In the second half we kept asking the defense to get us another stop. Eventually we had to give it something back, and we didn't.
The comeback began with stops

The Eclipse did not emerge from halftime with an instant offensive cure. Their first two possessions ended in punts. Medicham collected his fourth sack on the second, dropping Marino for six yards on third-and-seven. He finished with nine pressures as well as those four sacks. Verrick Brooks' absence did not leave Saffron without a disruptive linebacker. Medicham was the best argument against that assumption all afternoon.

Mossdeep's defense bought the offense time. Saffron's first two second-half possessions also ended in punts, gaining one yard and six yards respectively. Ray Glewis broke up a short throw on the first series. Luvrelle Revis limited a Skattebo run to one yard. On the next, Joey Sporeter and Ronnie Watt made the tackles before Manning threw the ball away on third-and-four. Those are small events until the offense needs six more chances to get itself organized.

The first Eclipse touchdown finally arrived on a six-play, sixty-seven-yard drive. Steel caught a sixteen-yard short-right pass. BeckhmJr followed with thirty-two yards deep right and eleven more short right. After a Ninjaskamara run and an incompletion, Marino found BeckhmJr short left for five yards on third-and-five. At 17–13, with 1:37 left in the third quarter, the game had become manageable without becoming comfortable.

Then the teams exchanged the sort of opportunities that make coaches repeat themselves. Armaldo Pace sacked Manning for eight yards. Later in that possession, Skattebo fumbled and Berry recovered. Two plays after Mossdeep took over, Richard Furman fumbled on a run up the middle, with Octillery recovering for Saffron. Nobody earned a touchdown from the exchange. The Eclipse had gained a chance and immediately returned it.

The defense answered again. Shawn Mareman sacked Manning for five yards near the end of the third quarter. Glewis stopped Skattebo for a three-yard loss to open the fourth. Druddamukong then sacked Manning for eight more on third-and-eighteen. That sequence erased the value of Saffron's recovery. Mossdeep's offense could be frustrated with itself while still receiving another possession within one score.

body.speaker: Electric Berry
body.text: The fumble was Ronnie's work before it was mine. I just tried to be there. On the interception, I saw the throw and got to it. It's easier talking about it after the clock stops.
The drive that mattered used both halves of the offense

Saffron's last serious chance to protect the lead began with Mothel Irving's thirty-two-yard catch. It reached another third down, but Manning's deep-right throw to Pickens fell incomplete on third-and-eight. Vikavolt punted into the end zone. Mossdeep took over at its twenty with 1:48 left, trailing by four. A field goal would have been useful earlier. It was no longer the assignment.

Marino opened with two throws to Ninjaskamara: seven yards short right, then nineteen deep left. BeckhmJr gained twenty-two more on a deep-right completion. Those three catches moved the drive quickly, but Dorrill's offense didn't turn the rest into a frantic throwing contest. Ninjaskamara carried four consecutive times, gaining four, ten, ten and two yards. The back who finished with seventy-eight rushing yards made twenty-six of them count on this possession.

On second-and-six, with forty-nine seconds showing, Marino went short right to BeckhmJr for the touchdown. Vinathorn added the extra point. Marino finished seventeen-of-twenty-six for 218 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He had endured four sacks and several stalled possessions. When Mossdeep needed an eighty-yard answer, he completed all four passes on the drive, and Ninjaskamara kept the running game fully involved.

Saffron's response lasted one throw. Manning went deep left; Berry intercepted and returned it five yards. The quarterback's final line was twenty completions in twenty-eight attempts for 258 yards, two touchdowns and that one interception. It was a good afternoon with a disastrous final entry. Mossdeep still had to close the game, which Furman helped do with an eight-yard run right on third-and-two with thirty-nine seconds remaining.

The health report complicates the celebration. Flock is out five weeks. BeckhmJr has a minor injury entry with no remaining absence. Mossdeep now goes to Vermilion at 9–0; Saffron hosts Fortree at 7–2. The Eclipse have shown they can survive a contender's best stretch. Now they must replace a corner while preserving what worked after halftime. For this week, the final defensive instruction was fulfilled exactly: Manning threw, Berry caught it, and Saffron never got another snap.

art.alt: Accel BeckhmJr celebrates in Mossdeep colors after a touchdown.

articles.title: Five touchdown passes, three Timmy scores, and one last exhale
articles.dek: Rustboro held off Cinnabar 41–38 after a fourth quarter that produced forty-two points. Gibby Timmy dominated through the air; Philly supplied the final first down.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Rustboro's best offensive play of the closing two minutes was a run. That may seem an odd place to begin a game in which Porygon-Z threw five touchdown passes and Gibby Timmy caught three, but the Stone had already demonstrated how quickly they could score. What they needed at the end was to prevent Cinnabar from getting another turn. Philly ran right for eleven yards on second-and-six. Porygon-Z knelt twice. A 41–38 win could finally be filed without adding another scoring entry.

The Stone improved to 6–4 with their third consecutive victory. Cinnabar fell to 7–3 despite scoring twenty-eight points in the fourth quarter and outgaining Rustboro 405–377. Porygon-Z completed sixteen of twenty-five throws for 268 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. Timmy caught seven passes for 157 yards, with touchdown receptions of thirty-three, ten and forty-six yards. He also returned a kickoff seventy-five yards to create another score. Cinnabar's pass defense and kick coverage both struggled to contain him.

Tyler Scarboro's team led 20–3 at halftime and 27–10 after three quarters. Neither lead survived as a comfortable arrangement. The final period included two one-play Stone touchdown drives, a ninety-seven-yard Cinnabar kickoff-return touchdown, three failed Blaze onside kicks, a missed extra point and a successful two-point conversion. The scoreboard was busy enough. The closing first down was a welcome change of subject.

body.speaker: Gibby Timmy
body.text: I liked the part where they had to kick it to us again. That's another chance to make the afternoon irritating. Three touchdowns is nice, but getting that last first down saved us from having to find a fourth.
Rustboro built the lead before the fireworks

The opening possessions were comparatively ordinary. Gorebyss made a forty-two-yard field goal. Tatsugiri intercepted Porygon-Z's next first-down throw, and Charjabug's twenty-nine-yarder tied the game at three. Rustboro limited the cost of its early turnover to a field goal. Cinnabar had tied the score, but its offense had finished another possession short of the end zone.

Rustboro's first touchdown drive supplied the foundation for everything that followed: twelve plays, seventy-six yards and repeated ground work. My Way, Son began it with a sixteen-yard run. Philly carried the middle of the possession, including an eight-yard gain up the middle on fourth-and-one. He converted another short situation before Porygon-Z found Lombre short left for a five-yard touchdown with 3:04 left in the second quarter. For a team about to produce so many explosive passes, the willingness to sustain this drive mattered.

Seismitoad fumbled on Cinnabar's ensuing possession. Smoke Break recovered, and the Stone added Gorebyss' thirty-three-yard field goal. The offense gained only two yards after the takeaway, so this was not a perfect exploitation of the chance. It still moved the score to 13–3. Cinnabar then punted again, leaving Rustboro another late-half opportunity with a lead already established.

Porygon-Z needed four plays to cover sixty-six yards. Gengar caught an eleven-yard pass; SEARED BITE followed with twenty-two yards down the left side. An incompletion preceded Timmy's thirty-three-yard touchdown on a deep-right throw with 1:03 left. The Stone took a seventeen-point advantage into halftime. They had scored through a long ground-based possession, a short field after a turnover, and a quick passing drive. Cinnabar had several different problems to address.

body.speaker: Tyler Scarboro
body.text: The long drive mattered as much as the quick ones. Philly kept us moving when we had to earn the next down. At the end we needed the same thing again: keep the ball, get the first down, finish.
Timmy kept finding the expensive answer

Cinnabar began the second half with a three-play, seventy-three-yard touchdown drive. Gholdengo's sixty-one-yard deep-right completion to Exploud set up Seismitoad's nine-yard scoring run left. It was an immediate reminder that the Blaze could move the game in large pieces too. The margin fell to ten, and Rustboro's next possession ended in a punt. At that point the comeback was more than an abstract possibility.

The Stone defense forced a punt on Cinnabar's next series. Rustboro then traveled seventy-seven yards in seven plays, surviving two third downs through the air. SEARED BITE gained fifteen on third-and-nine. Timmy gained forty-eight on third-and-seven, then caught a ten-yard deep-right touchdown on the very next snap. Those consecutive catches explain his afternoon more clearly than a general claim about speed: he supplied the drive's longest gain and immediately finished the opportunity it created.

SEARED BITE's forty-eight receiving yards deserve to remain in the account alongside Timmy's larger total. The fifteen-yard third-down catch prevented the series from ending before the forty-eight-yard play. Gengar added three catches for fifty-six yards and a touchdown, while Lombre's single target became the first Stone touchdown. Porygon-Z used the supporting receivers well enough that Cinnabar could not solve the game merely by acknowledging who was having the biggest day.

The quarterback also went the entire afternoon without being sacked. So did Gholdengo. This was a game decided through completions, coverage, returns and finishing rather than one quarterback repeatedly retreating under pressure. Cinnabar's passer attempted forty-five throws and completed twenty-seven for 325 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Those numbers were substantial. Rustboro's five passing touchdowns were more immediately valuable.

body.speaker: Porygon-Z
body.text: We had the time to find the next throw. The receivers finished the chances. Late in the game I wanted the ball to stay with us. Philly made that simple.
Forty-two fourth-quarter points did not change the winner

Seismitoad's three-yard rushing touchdown early in the fourth quarter brought Cinnabar within ten again. Timmy returned the kickoff seventy-five yards to the Blaze nineteen. Porygon-Z promptly found Gengar deep over the middle for a nineteen-yard touchdown. Rustboro's offense had used one snap to restore the seventeen-point margin. Timmy's contribution to that score did not appear in his receiving total, but it was plainly visible in the starting field position.

Gholdengo answered with an eight-play, eighty-two-yard drive, ending in an eight-yard short-right touchdown to Skiploom. Charjabug missed the extra point wide left. The Blaze tried an onside kick; SEARED BITE recovered at the Cinnabar forty-six. On the next snap, Porygon-Z went deep left to Timmy for all forty-six yards. Gorebyss' extra point put Rustboro ahead 41–23 with 3:52 remaining. That looked like enough separation. It lasted for one kickoff.

Archaludon took that kickoff ninety-seven yards for a touchdown. Cinnabar was back within eleven after the extra point. The Blaze tried another onside kick, which Aggron recovered for Rustboro. This time the Stone did not convert the short field into points. Two incomplete throws to SEARED BITE followed a short run, and Gorebyss punted into the end zone. Cinnabar had the ball back with 3:04 left, needing two scores and receiving another opportunity to make everyone uncomfortable.

Gholdengo moved the Blaze eighty yards in eleven plays. Frogadier supplied catches of nineteen and nine yards. Buizel added twelve and eighteen. Mawile caught a seven-yard short-left pass, then scored from four yards on third-and-three. Seismitoad ran up the middle for the two-point conversion. The score was 41–38 with 1:51 remaining, and Rustboro's eighteen-point lead had become a three-point problem.

Pupitar recovered Cinnabar's third onside attempt. Porygon-Z found Timmy short right for four yards, and Philly followed with the eleven-yard run that allowed the kneels. The Blaze never received the final possession they had spent the quarter trying to manufacture. They produced more first downs and more yards than Rustboro, but the Stone recovered every onside attempt and kept the last meaningful series in their own hands.

Cinnabar's 38 points were its best argument and its most frustrating number: enough offense to win many afternoons, insufficient compensation for five touchdown passes allowed. Rustboro can enjoy the victory while reviewing how a 41–23 lead became a live contest. Both clubs have a Week 11 bye. My Way, Son is listed out one week; his thirty-nine rushing yards came on five carries, while Philly finished with sixty-six on seventeen. The break arrives with the Stone fifth in the current Hoenn–Sinnoh playoff order and the Blaze fourth in Kanto–Johto. For Rustboro, the useful closing picture is still Philly going right, eleven yards gained, and the passing show finally allowed to end.

art.alt: Gibby Timmy rises for a catch in Rustboro brown and silver.

articles.title: The Reds leave no invitation: 34–0, and nine straight
articles.dek: Tic Thorpe accounted for four touchdowns as Mt. Silver returned from its bye, collected four Canalave turnovers and stayed unbeaten. Six catches on six targets made Scep Smith Jr. the drive-saving constant.
articles.author: rowan-vale

body.text: Canalave had a respectable record, a useful defense and the visitors coming off a week without a game. Mt. Silver responded by treating every loose ball as a delivery addressed to the Reds. Four Bulwark turnovers became twenty points, Tic Thorpe accounted for four touchdowns, and a 34–0 road win moved Connor McLarren's team to 9–0. The welcome-back party was rather one-sided. Canalave apparently supplied the gifts.

Thorpe threw for 281 yards and three touchdowns, completing twenty-one of thirty-three passes without an interception. He added a one-yard rushing score. The Reds outgained the Bulwark 366–154, converted seven of thirteen third downs, and held Canalave to seven first downs. Mt. Silver now has 239 points scored and 68 allowed. The undefeated record is eye-catching; the repeated refusal to let opponents assemble an answer is what makes it persuasive.

There were enough contributors to prevent this from becoming a quarterback biography. Scep Smith Jr. caught all six of his targets for sixty-four yards. Tony Gyarzalez caught five passes for seventy-seven and a touchdown. Gregar Jenings caught all three of his targets for fifty-three and a score. Tentacool added fifty yards and a touchdown. Tauros Woodson intercepted a pass and recovered a fumble. Kevin Metwae recovered two fumbles, including one that kept an early Reds possession alive. Everybody seemed to have been assigned a useful errand.

body.speaker: Kevin Metwae
body.text: If it's on the ground, I'm going after it. We recovered ours, then we recovered theirs. You don't need a complicated explanation for why that helps.
An early escape became an immediate touchdown

Mt. Silver's opening possession was not an immaculate demonstration. Raticate fumbled on the second play, and Metwae recovered. Delcatty then sacked Thorpe for seven yards. The Reds eventually punted after two Vibrava runs failed to undo the lost ground. Canalave had forced the stop it needed. Then Sneasel fumbled on the punt return, and Metwae recovered again, this time giving his offense the ball in scoring position.

Thorpe needed one play. He threw deep right to Jenings for a twenty-three-yard touchdown with 4:12 left in the first quarter. Two fumbles had occurred, but only Canalave's changed possession. The difference between keeping the first one and taking the second was a seven-point lead. Metwae's busy few minutes deserve more than a quiet note beneath the passing totals.

The Bulwark moved the ball on the ground during their first offensive series. Gabite gained six, one, five and four yards on consecutive carries. Then two Deerling runs lost a combined three yards, and Canalave punted. Those first four carries were encouraging enough to show a path. The next two showed how quickly that path could narrow when the offense needed another conversion.

Mt. Silver answered with a proper long drive, seventy-six yards in eight plays. Gyarzalez opened with an eight-yard reception. Jenings moved the chains, Smith gained fourteen on third-and-four, and Plusico Buress caught a nineteen-yard deep-left pass. With three seconds left in the quarter, Thorpe found Gyarzalez deep right for a nineteen-yard touchdown. The Reds had scored from a turnover-created short field and then from their own twenty-four. Canalave could not blame the whole deficit on the return mishap.

body.speaker: Connor McLarren
body.text: The recoveries gave us opportunities. The next job was to make those opportunities count, and the offense did that. We also had long drives where we earned the field ourselves. I liked that we could do both.
The completions that kept the afternoon moving

Smith's perfect six-for-six receiving line was not decorative efficiency. His fourteen-yard catch kept the second touchdown drive alive. In the second quarter he converted third-and-eight with nine yards. Later he supplied gains of ten and thirteen to help the Reds continue moving. There were no enormous numbers attached to any one catch, which is precisely why a defense can spend an afternoon feeling that it is almost off the field and still never get there.

Canalave's first pass of the second quarter made that problem worse. Slowking went deep left, and Woodson intercepted, returning the ball fourteen yards. Mt. Silver's offense gained seven yards on the ensuing series, enough for Adam Venutieri to make a fifty-three-yard field goal. It was 17–0. The Reds had turned their first two takeaways into ten points without asking either possession to be especially long.

The next Reds drive came close to adding more. Thorpe converted third downs to Smith and Jenings, then found Vulpix for another first down. Three consecutive incompletions toward Nuzleaf stopped the progress, the last two broken up by Weezing and Medicham. Canalave then produced a special-teams answer. Froslass blocked Venutieri's thirty-one-yard attempt with forty-eight seconds left in the half. A defense still waiting for its offense to score had at least kept three more points away.

Canalave promptly lost the ball again. Slowking was sacked and fumbled with twenty-seven seconds remaining, and Scizor recovered for Mt. Silver. Thorpe found Gyarzalez for five yards and Tentacool for twenty-one on third-and-five. Venutieri made a twenty-yard field goal with seven seconds left. The blocked kick had saved three points briefly. The turnover returned them before halftime. The Bulwark went to the break trailing 20–0, with no scoring possession of their own.

body.speaker: Scep Smith Jr.
body.text: Six targets, six catches is the standard I wanted today. The third downs are the part I care about. If the ball comes my way there, I expect us to keep playing.
Fourth down made the lead larger

Gabite began the third quarter with a seven-yard run, then gained ten more before fumbling. Woodson recovered. The running back ultimately finished with eighty-six yards on sixteen carries, an average of 5.4, but productive rushing cannot help the scoreboard when a drive ends by handing the ball away. Canalave had lost its fourth possession through a turnover before the half had settled into a rhythm.

Mt. Silver used ten plays and forty-eight yards to turn that recovery into another touchdown. Vibrava did much of the ground work, including an eleven-yard run and a four-yard conversion on third-and-three. The series eventually reached fourth-and-two. McLarren kept the offense on, and Thorpe threw short right to Tentacool for an eight-yard score with 3:24 left in the third quarter. Venutieri's extra point went in off the upright. At 27–0, even the narrow successes belonged to the visitors.

Tentacool finished with three catches for fifty yards. Two went for twenty-one yards; the third was that fourth-down touchdown. It was an economical afternoon in the best sense. Gyarzalez later provided a thirty-eight-yard deep-left catch on third-and-ten, moving the Reds close enough for Thorpe to finish from one yard out with 3:05 left. Their final touchdown required another difficult conversion before the short scoring play. The easy-looking end came after the hard part had already been completed.

Canalave did have defenders worth separating from the final score. Delcatty recorded all three sacks of Thorpe, including consecutive seven-yard losses early in the fourth quarter. Weezing made eleven tackles and forced a fumble. Froslass blocked a kick. Those contributions are real. They also underline how little offensive help arrived: Slowking finished eight-of-fifteen for sixty-three passing yards, with one interception, and the Bulwark never attempted a field goal.

The Reds' running totals were less spectacular than their passing ones, but they supplied enough help. Vibrava carried eleven times for forty-seven yards; Raticate added thirty-seven on eleven carries. They did not need to win the game by themselves. Their job was to keep possessions useful around Thorpe's completions, and Vibrava's third-and-three conversion on the third-quarter touchdown drive was a particularly clear example. The Reds could ask several different players for the next small piece.

The health report gives both teams work beyond the score. Jenings is out two weeks for Mt. Silver, taking a productive receiver out of the next matchup. Canalave linebacker Octillery is out six weeks. The Reds have other receivers who contributed here, but losing a player who caught all three targets is still an unwelcome item on McLarren's winning itinerary.

Byron's team fell to 6–4 and sixth in the current Hoenn–Sinnoh playoff order. It visits Olivine next. Mt. Silver remains the first Kanto–Johto seed and hosts a 6–3 Eterna team that has allowed seventy-seven points through nine games. That meeting offers a more interesting question than whether the Reds remembered how to play after the bye. They answered that one quickly. Canalave's final score was zero, and its four turnovers had supplied Mt. Silver twenty points before the last touchdown ever arrived.

art.alt: Tic Thorpe leads a crimson-clad group away from a waterfront field.

articles.title: Hobbes gave Lavender a head start. Pastoria kept the ball moving.
articles.dek: A 76-yard punt return supplied the Wails’ only touchdown in a 17–7 loss. Togekiss and Farigiraf helped Pastoria end a five-game skid while Lavender dropped its fourth straight.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: For a little while, Lavender had the kind of gift a struggling team hopes will change the afternoon. Hobbes fielded a punt at the Wails' twenty-four and returned it seventy-six yards for a touchdown. The defense had already recovered a fumble. A road game against another team searching for a win had begun with Lavender ahead, its returner doing the long-distance work and its offense being asked only to contribute something useful alongside him.

The offense never scored. Pastoria won 17–7, ending a five-game losing streak and sending the Wails to their fourth consecutive defeat. Lavender fell to 4–5 and outside the current seven Kanto–Johto playoff places. Pastoria improved to 3–6. Neither record invites extravagant conclusions, but this was an afternoon when one team found enough connected plays to change its recent story and the other kept finding isolated reasons to hope.

Togekiss completed twenty of twenty-nine passes for 230 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. Farigiraf caught six for eighty-nine yards and the touchdown that finally gave the Waves a two-score lead. Lavender's Mr. Clanky finished nine-of-twenty-six for ninety-six yards, no touchdowns and one interception. The Wails converted one of nine third downs. I can be patient about a season without pretending those numbers describe a functioning afternoon.

body.speaker: Hobbes
body.text: Seventy-six yards is a nice number to have attached to your name. I'd trade the interesting number for a boring win. We had plenty of game left after that return, and we needed something else to happen.
The early lead asked for a companion

Pastoria's opening possession ended when Watchog fumbled on a five-yard run right, with Picasso recovering for Lavender. The Wails immediately had a chance to turn the takeaway into points. Diggersby lost a yard, then Mr. Clanky threw two incompletions toward Beedrill. Just a cactus punted into the end zone. It was the first example of a pattern that became harder to excuse as the game continued: the defense could create a chance, but the offense still had to do something with it.

The Waves went three plays before punting on their next possession. Hobbes supplied the return touchdown, and Just a cactus added the extra point. Lavender led 7–0. A seventy-six-yard scoring run through a punt return is a major contribution on its own terms. It does not become less impressive because the offense later failed. It does become lonely on the scoring summary.

Lavender's defense forced another punt after Parasect sacked Togekiss for seven yards. The offense then produced its most encouraging early stretch, a nine-play possession that gained sixty yards. Diggersby had a twelve-yard run; Mr. Clanky added runs of seven and eight. Beedrill caught a fifteen-yard short-right pass, and Carnivine contributed on the ground and through the air. There was a recognizable sequence here, enough different pieces moving together to suggest the early lead might acquire some substance.

It ended on the first play after a short Carnivine completion opened the second quarter. Mr. Clanky threw deep left and Dubwool intercepted with 5:39 remaining in the half. Pastoria took over and drove eighty yards in twelve plays. Deerling finished with a three-yard run up the middle at the two-minute warning. Horsea's extra point tied the game. Lavender's best sustained early possession had become the beginning of Pastoria's best sustained early possession.

body.speaker: Travis Scarboro
body.text: We got the return, we got the takeaway, and we had a drive where we were moving it. Those were chances to build the game we wanted. We didn't finish enough of them, and we can't keep asking the defense and return game to cover that.
Pastoria found the passes its run game could not provide

The Waves' tying drive illustrates why the final passing difference mattered. Farigiraf caught passes of seven, sixteen and eleven yards during the possession. Kilowattrel added eleven. Other completions went to Watchog, Phanpy and Seel. Deerling's three-yard touchdown was the finishing touch, but a succession of completed throws had done much of the traveling. Pastoria did not need a dominant rushing afternoon to assemble a complete scoring drive.

It did not have one. Watchog carried fourteen times for twenty-nine yards. The Waves finished with forty-two rushing yards on twenty-three attempts, including Togekiss' kneels. Lavender's front repeatedly made running difficult. Mauler Twin recorded four tackles and two for loss, while Gumshoos and Stunfisk each made five tackles. Those efforts helped keep the score tied at halftime. They were useful work, not a complete solution to an offense stuck on seven points.

Pastoria's receivers gave Togekiss more reliable alternatives. Arbok caught four of five targets for seventy yards. Kilowattrel caught all five targets for thirty-six. Farigiraf's six receptions came on eight targets. Across the field, Beedrill caught three of twelve for twenty-seven yards, while Samurott had no catches on five targets. Those are not verdicts on the players' seasons or careers. They are the routes this particular game offered and the starkly different results they produced.

body.speaker: Mr. Clanky
body.text: There were throws we needed and didn't complete. The interception ended a drive that was working. I don't have a better description than that. We have to make the next down easier, and today we kept leaving ourselves the hard one.
Three failed fourth downs closed the remaining doors

The second half began with Lavender trying to take control of a manageable situation. Diggersby gained three yards, lost one, and Mr. Clanky found Beedrill for seven. On fourth-and-one, the quarterback ran right and Aggron stopped him for no gain. Pastoria took over, moved sixteen yards and kicked a thirty-yard field goal. Horsea had given the Waves their first lead, 10–7, with 3:49 left in the third quarter.

Lavender still had time, and its defense continued to supply opportunities. Pastoria later tried fourth-and-one itself, throwing incomplete toward Gumshoos. The Wails took possession and began a fifty-yard drive. Frosmoth caught a twenty-seven-yard deep-left pass. People Eater added fourteen on third-and-five. Those were substantial gains in a game where Lavender finished with only 160 total yards. Once again, there was enough movement to make the ending particularly frustrating.

The final three plays of that possession gained three yards: a short completion to Luvdisc, a Diggersby run for no gain, and an incomplete fourth-and-seven throw to Beedrill as the fourth quarter began. Lavender remained within a field goal. It also remained unable to convert its more promising stretches into even that field goal. A team can spend a long time within reach while steadily using up the possessions required to reach anything.

Pincurchin then helped make the next Wails possession brief. Mr. Clanky's deep-right throw to Samurott was broken up by Pincurchin, a short-left attempt to Samurott was broken up by Arctibax, and a deep-left throw to Frosmoth was broken up by Pincurchin. Three incompletions, three recorded breakups, another punt. The Waves' defense did not need a sack to produce a clean stop. Pincurchin finished with three pass breakups; Appletun added two.

Pastoria finally created separation with seven plays and eighty-seven yards. Farigiraf gained fifteen short right. Gumshoos caught fourteen on second-and-twelve. Arbok added twenty-one down the left side. With 2:28 remaining, Togekiss threw short left to Farigiraf, who gained thirty-one yards and scored. Horsea made the extra point. The Waves led 17–7, and Lavender now needed two scoring possessions from an offense that had not produced one.

body.speaker: Farigiraf
body.text: I enjoyed the short pass becoming the long problem. We'd kept finding enough to move, and that one finally gave us some room. I wasn't interested in giving them another close ending.

Lavender's last possession ended with its third failed fourth down of the half, a short-right throw to Beedrill broken up by Watchog. Pastoria then used a five-yard Watchog run on third-and-five to reach the kneeling stage. The Waves go to Mahogany next; the Wails host Veilstone, another club needing a response after a loss. There is still room in the season for Lavender to recover. The immediate request is much smaller than a declaration about its future: after Hobbes carries the ball seventy-six yards, someone on offense needs to carry the score beyond seven.

art.alt: Hobbes looks toward the field from a quiet Lavender sideline.
